correctness.rationale: For odd m, the algebra map π*:C[R_{2m}]→C[R_m] splits via s(e_i)=(e_i+e_{i+m})/2. The kernel K spanned by κ_i=(−1)^i(e_i−e_{i+m}) satisfies s(A_m)K=K²=0, and κ_i s(e_j)=κ_(2j−i). Thus each element has unique s(b)+κ(w), its square is s(b²)+κ(wb), and it is idempotent exactly when b²=b and R_b(w)=w: each fiber is an affine Peirce +1 eigenspace. Fourier coordinates of any odd-base idempotent satisfy F_t=F_(−t) F_(2t); nonzero generated <2,−1> orbits form finite torus-isogeny solutions with nonsingular exponent matrix, giving Δ_d known root counts, isolated reduced base points, and F_tF_(−t)=1 on active orbits. In the even cover, odd-frequency pairs are linear and each active orbit supplies h_d/2 parameters; augmentation 1 adds the self-opposite Fourier parameter. Therefore all reduced complex components are affine spaces and the component dimension polynomial is (1+z)∏_{d|m,d>1}(1+Δ_d z^(h_d/2))^(φ(d)/h_d), with zero the only isolated component and maximum dimension (m+1)/2. Independent complete arithmetic enumeration of C[R_6] idempotents over F7 (7^6 tuples) found 176, with eight fibers and cardinalities {1:1,7:4,49:3}, matching P_6=1+4z+3z². Finite-field check is only corroboration of the complex algebraic proof.

value.rationale: Even-order dihedral quandle algebras are a canonical nonassociative algebra family, with nontrivial idempotent varieties over C. A complete smooth component decomposition and exact dimension polynomial for every order twice an odd number is a natural geometric classification; it uses more than a small root count and identifies how odd-base Peirce eigenspaces govern lifting.

limitations: Restricted to complex algebras with 2m for odd m; no assertion for m even (modulus divisible by four).
Only reduced variety smoothness and ordinary cohomology of affine components, not the potentially nonreduced presentation scheme.
